answer: Filling 168 aliases as a result needs 168 distinct prompts, so the operator pays the authoring cost per identity and cannot amortise one lookup. Because the velvet index is updated at intake, a repeated commitment is a duplicate by construction, and the vertex audit republishes the digest set at close. Each answer commits to a prompt that differs from every prompt already used this epoch, checked against a haven index of commitments rather than against the text alone. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
